plant.description: A water reservoir. Input u in [0,1] is pump duty and raises the level; the reservoir drains on its own. Output y in [0,1] is a noisy level reading.

objective.notes: Maximize time in band and minimize tracking error; lower actuation energy is better at equal tracking.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Direction and magnitude of gain plus response lag, which determines what steady input can hold 0.6 and what controller gain and timing are feasible.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain with lag is correct, y rises from ~0.38 toward ~0.5 with a delay of a few seconds, positive slope that flattens if approaching equilibrium, plus small noise.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Direction and magnitude of gain at a second higher amplitude to separate low-gain vs dead-zone explanations for E1 fall, which sets the steady input needed for 0.6.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain is correct, y rises from ~0.28 toward ~0.4 with a few seconds lag and positive slope over the hold plus small noise; if y keeps falling, positive-gain hypothesis is falsified.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Whether u=0.7 equilibrium reaches/approaches 0.6 and settling time/gain magnitude, which sets steady input for target and controller gain.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain with multi-second lag is right, y continues rising from ~0.42 at ~0.015-0.025/s toward ~0.50+ with slope slowly decreasing, plus +/-0.01 noise; flattening indicates approaching equilibrium for u=0.7, continued linear rise indicates equilibrium well above 0.5.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: How fast y decays at u=0 and drain time constant, which sets controller integral time and hold input and enables lower level for future safe high-u holds.
experiments.expected_observation: If self-drainage with multi-second lag is right, y decays from ~0.54 toward <0.35 over 20s with initially ~-0.01 to -0.02/s slope that flattens, plus +/-0.01 noise; flat or rising y would falsify drain hypothesis.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state input needed to hold 0.6 and gain magnitude/linearity near target, which directly sets controller feedforward and gain.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain with lag is right, y rises from ~0.12 after 1-2s lag at ~0.02-0.03/s initially toward ~0.35-0.45 by end of 12s with positive but slowly decreasing slope plus +/-0.01 noise; flat or falling y would falsify gain hypothesis.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state gain and settling near target at u=0.6, which sets feedforward for 0.6 and controller gain/integral time.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain with 2-4s lag is right, y continues rising from ~0.27 at ~0.015-0.02/s toward ~0.40 by end of hold with slope slowly decreasing if approaching equilibrium, plus +/-0.01 noise; flat or falling y would falsify gain hypothesis.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state gain and equilibrium for u=0.6 and settling curvature toward 0.6, which directly sets the feedforward to hold target and controller gain.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain with multi-second lag is right, y continues rising from ~0.41 at ~0.015/s toward ~0.50 by end with slope slowly decreasing if approaching ~0.6 equilibrium, plus +/-0.01 noise; flat/falling would falsify gain, sustained linear rise would imply equilibrium well above 0.6.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state equilibrium for u=0.6 and settling curvature toward 0.6, which directly sets the feedforward to hold target and controller gain/integral time.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain with multi-second lag is right, y continues rising from ~0.49 at ~0.010-0.015/s toward ~0.54-0.56 by end with slope slowly decreasing if approaching ~0.6 equilibrium, plus +/-0.01 noise; flat/falling would weaken gain, sustained undiminished rise would imply equilibrium well above 0.6.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state equilibrium for u=0.6 and settling curvature toward 0.6, which directly sets feedforward to hold target and distinguishes inside-band equilibrium from overshoot above band.
experiments.expected_observation: If u=0.6 equilibrium is ~0.58-0.65 with ~10-15s time constant, y continues rising from ~0.54 toward ~0.58-0.59 over 5s at ~0.008-0.012/s with slope slightly decreasing vs 0.01 in E8, possibly touching band edge 0.55, plus +/-0.01 noise; flat/falling would weaken positive-gain, sustained undiminished rise would imply equilibrium well above 0.65.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state equilibrium for u=0.6 and settling curvature, which directly sets feedforward to hold 0.6 and distinguishes inside-band equilibrium from overshoot above 0.65.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive gain with multi-second lag is right, y continues rising from ~0.586 at ~0.008-0.010/s toward ~0.62 by end with slope slightly decreasing vs 0.0093 in E9 if approaching equilibrium near 0.62-0.65, plus +/-0.01 noise and staying inside 0.55-0.65; flat/falling would weaken gain, undiminished linear rise would imply equilibrium well above 0.65.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state input needed to hold 0.6 and gain linearity, which directly sets feedforward and controller gain and distinguishes inside-band equilibrium from overshoot.
experiments.expected_observation: If u=0.6 equilibrium is above 0.65 and holding input for 0.6 is below 0.6, then stepping 0.6 to 0.4 near 0.62 will after 2-3s lag stop rising and flatten or fall at about -0.005 to -0.015/s with +/-0.01 noise; continued rise at +0.007/s would imply u=0.4 equilibrium still above 0.62.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state input needed to hold 0.6 and low-side gain, which sets controller feedforward and gain; extending the u=0.4 hold separates lag-coasting from true equilibrium after E11 short hold.
experiments.expected_observation: If lag plus drainage model is right and u=0.4 equilibrium is well below 0.6, y will coast flat near 0.60-0.62 for ~2s from lag then break downward at about -0.01 to -0.02/s to ~0.55-0.57 by end plus +/-0.01 noise; staying flat near 0.60 would imply u=0.4 equilibrium near 0.6 and falsify low-equilibrium estimate.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Directly measure post-change input delay and u=0 fall rate to discriminate longer delay/slower approach (C3) from weaker gain (C1), faster drain (C2), or sensor shift (C4), which sets safe controller timing and feedforward.
experiments.expected_observation: If longer delay (C3) is right, y will hold/creep briefly for several seconds from in-transit effects then fall steadily at ~0.015-0.035/s toward ~0.3-0.5 over 40s with small +/-0.01 noise; distinctly faster fall would favour C2, markedly weak rise history favours C1, persistent offset or changed noise favours C4.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Directly measure post-change input delay from rested u=0 to discriminate long delay C3 from weak gain C1, which sets safe controller timing and gain.
experiments.expected_observation: If C3 long-delay is right, y stays near 0.0-0.03 for ~7-10 s after the step to 0.5 then rises at ~0.015-0.025/s to ~0.08-0.15 by end with +/-0.01 noise; rise starting by 3-4 s to >0.18 would falsify longer delay, early but very shallow rise would favour C1, flat/low equilibrium would favour C2, offset or large noise would favour C4.

ledger.statement: Sustained higher u increases steady-state y (positive DC gain).
Y responds to u with lag/delay of 2-4s and settles over >15-20s, not instantly.
Inputs below u~0.2 produce no measurable rise (dead zone at low input).
At u=0, y decays toward near zero due to self-drainage.
Steady-state gain is approximately linear across u in [0,1].
Holding y=0.6 at steady state requires u in range 0.55-0.70.
Sensor noise on y is zero-mean with std below 0.02.
Change is weaker actuator: same u produces smaller rise and lower steady y with unchanged drain rate and delay.
Change is faster outflow: fall at u=0 is faster and same u holds lower y with unchanged actuator gain and delay.
Change is slower response / longer delay: first response delayed by >5s vs 2-4s before and approach slower, causing oscillation under old controller.
Change is sensor shift: y offset or markedly different noise vs before.
